title: A Provision for the Current
premise: Ivo Sandoval, a bush pilot who ferries medicine and gossip along the Vessarin River, has spent years outrunning a name they no longer answer to. When a flood delivers a sealed chest bearing the crest of Karavel—a nation erased from every map—Ivo is pulled into a race against surveyors, smugglers, and an old friend turned government agent to reach the river's forbidden source before it can be dammed and its last free settlement drowned. Along the way Ivo gathers a ragged found family: a disgraced cartographer, a stowaway girl who claims the chest as inheritance, and a mechanic with debts of her own. In the end Ivo must choose between destroying the evidence that would restore their own identity or using it to prove the source belongs to no nation at all—and chooses truth over safety, grounding their plane for good.
about_author: Coral Coldharbour spent a decade ferrying supplies on remote waterways before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the salt-rot and engine-oil honesty of those years. She writes from a houseboat she refuses to anchor in any one country.

chapters.title: Cargo and Rumor
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine supply run down the Vessarin establishes Ivo's restless life: medicine drops, whispered news, a plane held together by stubbornness. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as freedom—every stop is warm, and every departure is relief.

chapters.title: What the Flood Returned
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. After a storm, the river coughs up a lead-lined chest stamped with Karavel's seal—impossible, since Karavel was erased decades ago. Inside are documents naming a 'provision' hidden at the source. Fear arrives first: someone will come asking questions.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Claimed It
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. A teenage stowaway emerges from Ivo's cargo hold and claims the chest belonged to her grandmother, a Karaveli exile. Her certainty forces Ivo to admit the chest means something personal too. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual secrets.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Ivo seeks out Marta Okonkwo, a drunk ex-surveyor who once mapped the upper river before being discredited. She recognizes the seal and warns that a corporate survey fleet is already heading upstream to dam the source. Beat: guilt rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Agent Reyes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An old comrade from Ivo's buried past arrives wearing a government badge, offering amnesty if Ivo surrenders the chest. Their history reveals fragments of who Ivo used to be. Beat: the past stops being avoidable; loyalty and truth begin to pull apart.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Fleet
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The four flee upstream through rapids and fog while the survey fleet's barges close behind. Nadia proves herself navigating channels only Karaveli pilots ever knew. Beat: the group becomes a crew; trust hardens under fire.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. They reach a hidden settlement of Karaveli descendants living off the record for generations. Nadia finds family she never knew; Ivo sees what staying invisible costs. Beat: belonging offered freely, which terrifies Ivo more than any agent.

chapters.title: The Provision
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the source, the chest's final lock opens: not treasure but legal proof—a treaty granting the river's headwaters to the Karaveli people in perpetuity, buried when the nation was erased. Reyes's team arrives. Beat: triumph curdling into siege.

chapters.title: The Dam Breaks First
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The survey fleet begins blasting regardless of law; the village floods early and the crew rescues villagers through the night, Reyes among them after his orders turn lethal. Beat: loyalty tested—Reyes must choose his career or the people he once fought beside.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With the treaty broadcast from Ivo's plane radio and witnesses across three nations, the dam project collapses and the village wins recognition. Ivo signs their old name to the testimony—then chooses the new one anyway. Beat: identity reclaimed on Ivo's own terms; the found family stays.
